creator: brooke_wrightmode
title: Make a 'prompt-builder' skill in Claude (Customize > Skills) whose instruction makes Claude ask three clarifying questions (output contents, reader, what would make it wrong) before writing a structured prompt

tools.name: Claude (claude.ai) Customize > Skills
tools.detail: create a skill named prompt builder; invoke with 'use prompt-builder' in any new chat

claims: A skill is a set of instructions you say once and Claude knows how to do that task repeatedly
Claude will ask three questions then build a structured prompt, cutting back-and-forth guessing
how_to_steps: Open Claude, click Customize, then Skills
Create a skill with Claude and name it 'prompt builder'
Paste instruction: 'When I describe a task, ask me what the output needs to contain, who reads it, and what would make it wrong. Then write me a good prompt.'
Save; type your task in plain words
Claude asks three questions and returns a structured prompt
In any new chat say 'use prompt builder' to load it
on_screen_only: Sticker 'WORK SMARTER NOT HARDER'; cards 'INSTRUCTIONS' / 'SAVED ONCE'
Step chips: '1 Customize > Skills', '4 Save + type task', '5 Any'
Chat boxes: 'When I describe a task, ask...', 'Then write me a good prompt.', 'use prompt-builder'
cta: Comment 'build out' for the guide; save and follow

gap.what: Small but new technique: a clarifying-questions meta-skill (output, audience, failure mode) before generation. Liked set has 'Unlazy' and 'Context Transfer' prompts but not this intake pattern.

relevance.why: Consumer-level; Haji already writes briefs for Claude Code, though the three questions are a decent intake checklist for subagent prompts.

implement_score.why: Could fold the three questions into an existing brief/handoff skill in five minutes; not worth a standalone skill.

verify: Whether claude.ai 'Customize > Skills' matches the current UI naming
